mitigation_descriptions: Prevent adversary access to privileged accounts or access necessary to perform this technique. Consider removing and replacing system components suspected of being compromised.

Take measures to detect or prevent techniques such as OS Credential Dumping. Limit credential overlap across systems to prevent access if account credentials are obtained. Ensure that local administrator accounts have complex, unique passwords across all systems on the network. Audit domain and local accounts as well as their permission levels routinely.

Set account lockout policies after a certain number of failed login attempts to prevent passwords from being guessed. Use multifactor authentication. Follow best practices for mitigating access to Valid Accounts.
reasoning: The intranet-server suffered privilege escalation from www-data to gmorgan and root, culminating in credential dumping of /etc/shadow from a web directory. Immediate containment is necessary to stop further lateral movement and credential exploitation.
remediation_plan: 1. Isolate the intranet-server (192.168.104.155) from the network to prevent lateral movement and exfiltration. 2. Terminate unauthorized sessions and processes associated with user gmorgan and web service user www-data. 3. Prevent adversary access to privileged accounts by rotating credentials and password hashes for all accounts present in /etc/shadow. 4. Audit local and domain account permissions, sudoers configuration, and SSH keys to enforce least privilege. 5. Inspect and remove any webshells or malicious files deployed within the WordPress uploads directory. 6. Enforce multifactor authentication and limit credential overlap across systems to prevent credential reuse.
